title: Captain Arthur Taylor gets him sent home
summary: A Sergeant called him AWOL after a trip taking a Major to Brussels, but old Pittsburgh schoolmate Captain Arthur Taylor checked his points and sent him and his friends home.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: And there was a Captain who was assigned to our company whom I had went to school with in Pittsburgh, Captain Taylor, Arthur Taylor.
A black Captain.
Yeah. But I mean his mother was Danish.
Oh.
You know. He had big blue eyes and --
Fancy that.
But I knew his father. I knew his whole family, because we lived close together.
What an odd coincedence.
So he said to me one day -- I went to take a Major to Brussels.
Yeah.

So the Sergeant, when I -- I stayed about -- oh, I guess about 10 days, so when I returned, the Sergeant said, 'You're AWOL.' I said, 'What do you mean, AWOL? I was assigned to take the Major to Brussels.' He said, 'No, as far as I'm concerned you're AWOL, and you're going to be punished for it.' So he said, 'Captain, would you come out, please, sir? This AWOL has returned.' So the Captain walks out. He looks at me, he said, 'Kenny.' I said, 'Arthur.' So the Sergeant, he just dropped to his knees, because I was then -- so he said, 'What's wrong?' I said, 'This Sergeant's telling me I'm AWOL.' He said, 'Well, you took the --', 'When I arrived they told me you had taken a Major to Brussels.' I said, 'That's right, I did.' He said, 'Well, why is he AWOL.' The Sergeant didn't like me. Because we were musicians, you know.
Figured you were getting some privileges.

Yeah. So -- and then Arthur says to the Sergeant, he says, "Go get his dossier. Go get his papers. I want to see what Kenny -- Kenny, how long have you been here?" I said, "Too long, Arthur." You know. So he looked at it and he said, "Well, you have enough points to go home." So he sent me to a little town in Germany where I was supposed to take the train to catch the boat, and he sent me home.
Fancy that.

With all of my friends. He says, "Who do you want to go with you?" I says, "Well, him. Him." And we had Skeets Franklin, the bass player from Brooklyn -- yeah, he's from Brooklyn. And he was playing with us, so I said, "I want him, him, and --," and I took all my friends home with me.
What an extraordinary thing.
Isn't that something?
Isn't that? What an amazing thing.

So this Sergeant, he didn't know what to say. So he came over and started patting me and hugging me, and I said, "Don't hug me." You know. Because I know he wanted me to say a word for him to Captain Taylor, you know.
Yeah. What a funny -- and you didn't know that Taylor was there?
No, I didn't know because I had been away with the Major.
And he just got assigned.

He was just assigned while I was away, and when I returned, there he was, Captain Taylor. Oh, Captain Taylor. He said, 'Kenny, what are you doing here?' He says, 'You want to go home? Well, you have enough points. You have something like 57 points and you only need 55. Go home.'
And you might have been there a long time.
With that sergeant I would probably never have gotten out of the Army.
Yeah, fancy that. So he got you sent home, and how long did it take you to demob?
